summary: Completed WU14-07 evidence-based runtime optimization review without weakening refresh semantics.
completed: Reviewed the confirmed six-SSH-execution refresh candidate and rejected batching, data reuse, probe removal, multiplexing, and per-device collector parallelism because current evidence does not demonstrate a safe gain without coupling failure, timeout, capacity, or host-key behavior.
Added active-only successful SSH result-byte aggregation to the real and fake executors so deterministic profiles now report safe aggregate bytes without retaining payloads.
Re-ran the 2/5/10 deterministic profiles: request counts remain 12/30/60, failures remain zero, durations remain below aggregate millisecond resolution, and result bytes are 1080/2700/5400.

validationCommands.summary: Protects 2/5/10 request counts, zero SSH failures, and result-byte totals.
Canonical Rust/frontend/AIQT/diff validation passed; frontend lint retains four warnings.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Every optimization has a measured reason and result
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: The WU14-07 report records the before/after profile evidence and explicit safety rationale for every reviewed candidate; none met the acceptance bar.
The successful-refresh model remains six independently bounded SSH executions per device; monitoring cadence, query gates, failure isolation, and host-key verification are unchanged.
The deterministic profile regression now asserts request count, zero failures, and safe aggregate byte totals for all three profile sizes.

notes: Risk score: 14/100 (low): active-only diagnostics accounting and deterministic test coverage; no production request, timeout, scheduler, or parsing behavior changes.
Residual for WU14-08: live-device transport duration/connection setup and interactive GUI evidence remain unavailable; do not infer them from fixture timings.
